study.title: Frequency-Specific Blood Oxygen Level Dependent Oscillations Associated With Pain Relief From Ankle Acupuncture in Patients With Chronic Low Back Pain
study.study_design: Within-subject crossover design; participants received both tactile sham acupuncture (TSA) and ankle acupuncture stimulation (AAS) in pseudo-randomized order
study.randomization: The order of AAS and TSA runs was pseudo-randomized across subjects
study.blinding: Participants were acupuncture naïve and were informed that there would be 'different forms' of acupuncture during fMRI. The needles used for AAS and TSA were identical. Locations of needle stimulation were taped with medical adhesive tape. Participants lay supine with vision of distal body regions blocked by MRI head coil. Blinding success was validated at the end of the study.
study.population: 27 patients with CLBP and 25 age- and gender-matched healthy volunteers
study.inclusion_criteria: Patients: (1) right-handed adults of any gender aged 18 to 65 years; (2) a history of low back pain for 6 months or more; (3) an initial self-reported pain intensity evaluated using the visual analog scale (VAS, 0–10) of at least 4 points; (4) able to understand and complete the consent form and clinical assessment questionnaires without assistance. Healthy subjects: (1) right-handed, age- and gender-matched adults; (2) no history of pain or relevant serious disease; (3) able to understand and complete the consent form without assistance.
study.exclusion_criteria: Patients and healthy subjects: (1) the presence of another cause of pain unrelated to LBP; (2) having taken any medication or undergone physical therapy in the past week; (3) any other serious illnesses or neuropsychiatric diseases; (4) any contraindications for undergoing MRI, including the presence of metal implants, cardiac pacemakers, or claustrophobia; (5) any contraindications for undergoing acupuncture, such as pregnancy or a tendency to bleed easily; (6) a history of sleep deprivation or women who were experiencing their menstrual period; (7) having consumed coffee or alcohol in the 10 h prior to the MRI scan. Any individual who moved their head by more than 1 mm or 2° during the scan was excluded from the analyses.

arms.dropouts: 12 patients dropped out during the experimental period. Three participants could not tolerate the scanning session. Two participants were not imaged during acupuncture stimuli due to claustrophobia. Three participants terminated the study due to excessive fear. One subject was removed for suspected sub-clinical neuropathy. Three participants voluntarily withdrew. One patient was excluded because of severe head movement during fMRI.
One control was excluded because of severe head movement during fMRI.

conditions.timepoint_exact: During TSA stimulation run followed by 8 min rest scan
conditions.scan_context: Resting-state fMRI scan conducted after TSA stimulation (needles withdrawal), 8 min rest run
conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: The needle is explicitly described as inserted into the skin and angled horizontally into the subcutaneous layer, traveling approximately 35 mm toward the knee at ~30°. Despite the horizontal/subcutaneous trajectory and absence of induced sensation, the needle physically penetrates well beyond 5 mm into subcutaneous tissue, engaging deep cutaneous and subcutaneous mechanoreceptors. This constitutes full/deep penetration (Level 1).

extraction_notes.note: The fMRI scanning paradigm description (Figure 2) is somewhat ambiguous about exactly when the resting-state scans used for ALFF analysis were acquired. The paradigm shows Rest 1 (pre-TSA), TSA 8 min, Rest 2 (post-TSA), then 15 min structural/functional scan, then AAS 8 min, then Rest 3 (post-AAS). The text states rest runs were conducted after needles withdrawal. It is unclear whether ALFF was computed from the post-stimulation rest run (Rest 2 or Rest 3) or the stimulation run itself.

The Brodmann area entries in Table 2 for slow-3 and slow-2 bands contain apparent OCR artifacts (e.g., '13, 4, 7228, 3834, 8, 6' and '13, 4, 738, 2234, 6' and '23, 2730' and '13, 2234, 4144'). These appear to be OCR errors from a multi-column table cell. The values have been preserved as-is from the PDF but may not be accurate.

The abstract states 27 patients and 25 healthy controls were enrolled. The participants section in results states 52 participants (27 patients, 25 volunteers). After dropouts and exclusions, the final dataset was 19 patients and 19 healthy subjects. The abstract states 'Twenty seven patients with CLBP and Twenty five age- and gender-matched healthy volunteers' but the final analyzed N is 19 per group.
No formal deqi/needle sensation measurement instrument was used. The paper only states 'All the participants reported no obvious needle sensation during acupuncture' as a qualitative observation.
Expectancy ratings were not formally assessed. No credibility scale or expectancy measure was reported beyond the blinding validation statement.
Adverse events were not reported. No statement was made about whether adverse events occurred or were monitored.

The correlation analysis scatter plots in Figure 5 show MNI coordinates x=39, y=6, z=-21 for the right insula, but the main effects tables report the right insula peak at x=39, y=-6, z=21 (for Norm-1) or similar. The figure caption coordinates and table coordinates differ slightly across bands. The correlation figure explicitly states MNI: x=39, y=6, z=-21 for right insula. This discrepancy has been preserved as reported.

The MNI coordinates reported in Table 2 for the right insula in the Norm-1 row are listed as x=39, y=-6, z=21, but in the results text and Figure 5, the peak coordinate for right insula overlap is reported as x=39, y=6, z=-21. These may represent different cluster peaks or an OCR error in the table. Both values have been preserved as reported in their respective locations.
Supplementary Materials are referenced for the re-analysis using voxel level p < 0.001 but are not provided in this document. Results from supplementary materials were not extracted.

The group-level interaction (group × treatment) result is stated as 'zALFF within each frequency band did not show any statistically significant differences with the main effects of participant group or any interaction between group and treatment.' No coordinates are provided for these null results.

Several Brodmann area values in Table 2 appear to be OCR artifacts where multiple BA codes were concatenated (e.g., '4, 7228' likely means 'BA 4, 7, 22, 8' and '2234' likely means '22, 34'). These have been preserved verbatim from the PDF.

The cluster size for slow-3 Right insula row in Table 2 is listed as '13, 4,7228, 3,8348 6' in the BA column and '448' in cluster size. The BA column appears to concatenate multiple entries. Preserved as found in OCR extraction.

The study used a within-subject crossover design where both CLBP patients and healthy controls received both TSA and AAS. The main effects analysis collapsed across both groups. The group factor did not show a significant main effect or interaction. Therefore, neural contrasts reported primarily reflect condition effects (AAS vs TSA) across both groups combined.
